subject: MAP: unit economics alignment — caching & batching assumptions
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Sokolov <elena@quantahealth.com>, Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@quantahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-27T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: unit economics alignment — caching & batching assumptions

Hi Elena / Sam,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we start drafting the mutual action plan (MAP) and the evaluation milestones, a few unit-econ assumptions need to be explicit so your legal/procurement and our finance teams are aligned before the SOW. Attached: MAP_v1.xlsx and token-econ-summary.pdf.

Key asks for confirmation by EOD Tue:
- Target tokens per $ (or costs per 1k tokens) you expect us to model for the pilot and for production.
- Expected cache hit rate (prefix/KV hit) on your live traffic (ballpark %).
- Typical user session profile: avg prompt tokens vs avg completion tokens (or we can use your traffic CSV).
- Batching tolerance: acceptable extra latency if we batch to improve cost (we assume 8–12 avg batch size for background gen, 2–4 for interactive flows).

Our initial assumptions in the attached are:
- Cost target: ~$0.60 per 1k tokens (≈ 1,666 tokens/$) for the pilot (can discuss tradeoffs).
- Prefix/KV cache hit: 45% (conservative).
- Effective batching: avg 6 tokens/batch for interactive calls, 10 for async backfill.
- Eval plan: 2-week pilot (traffic shadowing), 1-week A/B quality check, then canary.

If you prefer, we can run a quick sensitivity table (tokens/$ vs cache hit vs batch size) and attach to the MAP.

Next steps: once you confirm the bullets above we’ll update MAP_v1 and send a clean SOW for procurement.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), token-econ-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Sokolov <elena@quantahealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-28T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: unit economics alignment — caching & batching assumptions

Hi Evelyn — thanks, this is helpful.

A few clarifications from our side:
- For the pilot we need to see a model that projects <=$0.65 per 1k tokens at our expected traffic profile; long term we’re targeting <$0.50/1k but pilot tolerance is wider.
- Our internal analytics team reports a ~52% reuse rate on standard prompts but that includes server-side dedupe; for an apples-to-apples prefix/KV cache hit we expect ~40% initially and hope to tune to 55% during pilot.
- Session profile: I’m attaching qh_traffic_profile.csv — typical scenario is 120 tokens prompt / 240 tokens completion average per session for our triage workflow; some review flows are 40/80.
- Latency SLAs: interactive flows need p95 < 450ms; p99 < 900ms. If batching adds >150ms we likely need fallback to a lower-cost fast model.

For the MAP, procurement will want a clear acceptance criteria table (tokens per $ assumptions, cache hit expectations, latency thresholds by route, and rollback/canary triggers). Can you add that to MAP_v1 and resend?

Thanks — will loop procurement once the SOW is in a near-final state.

Best,
Elena
Elena Sokolov
Head of AI Integrations, QuantaHealth
attachments: qh_traffic_profile.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-29T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP: unit economics alignment — caching & batching assumptions

Quick summary of the sensitivity run (attached SOW_draft.docx + a short table in-line):

Assumptions (applied to qh_traffic_profile.csv):
- Avg session: 120 prompt / 240 completion tokens (as provided).
- Baseline model cost: $0.60 per 1k tokens (our default compiled run).
- Caching: prefix/KV hit rates modeled at 40% (baseline), 55% (optimistic).
- Batching: interactive avg batch size = 4 (latency impact +30–70ms), async avg = 10 (saves ~22% token cost).

Sensitivity outcomes (pilot projection):
- Scenario A (40% cache, batch 4): effective tokens/$ ~1,500 -> cost ≈ $0.67 per 1k tokens.
- Scenario B (55% cache, batch 10): effective tokens/$ ~1,900 -> cost ≈ $0.53 per 1k tokens.
- Break-even to meet Elena’s <=$0.65/1k target: cache >= 43% with batching avg >=6 under current model kernels.

Operational notes:
- To hit p95 < 450ms for interactive flows we recommend an isolated low-latency pool (small model quantization + no batching) for the triage route and an async path (batched) for heavier review flows.
- Fallback plan: automatic routing to a cheaper 8-bit variant when queue latency > 600ms; canary policy: 10% traffic for 48h then 25% for 72h.

I attached SOW_draft.docx with the acceptance criteria table and the above guarantees (we used conservative headroom). If this looks good I’ll incorporate into MAP_v1.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: SOW_draft.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: MAP: unit economics alignment — caching & batching assumptions

Evelyn / team — this reads well. Procurement reviewed Ben’s sensitivity and SOW draft with our finance team. Two final asks before we sign:

1) Can Redwood commit to the following pilot acceptance criteria (we will run pilot with production-ish traffic):
  - Effective cost: <= $0.65 per 1k tokens (using our qh_traffic_profile.csv)
  - Prefix/KV cache: baseline >= 43% during pilot, target >=55% by pilot end
  - Latency: interactive p95 < 450ms; fallback route p95 < 700ms
  - Rollback: automated rollback to pre-deploy model if error rate > 1.2% or tail latency triggers for >12 hours
2) Pilot start target: Nov 15 (2-week pilot, then 1-week A/B). SOW signature by Nov 8 to hit that start date.
If Redwood can include a short note in the SOW about an agreed measurement script (we’ll run a joint evaluation harness to validate token counts and cache hit reporting), procurement is comfortable advancing.
Assuming acceptance, we’ll have procurement sign and send counterparty redlines to Marissa.
Thanks,
Elena

--
